ai.description: This snake reaches 25–30 cm. It is glossy dark brown with a yellow-spotted underside and a small, pointed head. The tail ends in a flat, circular, heavily keeled shield.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis nitida* is best distinguished by its smooth, glossy scales and the presence of a distinct, sharply keeled, shield-like terminal scale at the tip of its tail.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis nitida* inhabits the moist evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Uropeltis nitida* is primarily nocturnal, spending its time burrowing through moist soil and leaf litter in search of earthworms and other soft-bodied invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis nitida* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis nitida* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests above 1,000 meters.
